pairs.why: B's mid-key, more saturated green with a darker rim sits nearer the real card's medium key, while A's pale, glowing yellow-green corner brightens the card and flattens the hero separation.
B's large dark navy fixture forms a big dark mass against the mid-value teal as in the real card, while A's small dark body is lost in a bright cyan field.
Both are the same pale grey-lavender, low-contrast and high-key moon scene with equal value grouping, so value gives no reason to choose.

A's mostly dark navy hero, with only a few bright cyan accents against yellow-orange, a centre glow and darker orange corners, matches the real card, whereas B's cream keys add much harder local contrast.
Both have the same bright cream wall, saturated blue door and similar ivy darks, and neither is noticeably closer to the real card's deeper shadowed key.
A keeps the real card's bright, high-key airy sky and softly graded silver-blue hero, while B is slightly darker with a heavier tiled-floor mass.
A's darker wall behind the hat and heavy cast shadow on the left are closer to the real card's low-key, shadowed room than B's lighter floor and wall.
Both use a darker, more saturated magenta than the real card's lighter pink with a similar centre glow and edge darkening, so value gives no reason to choose.
